newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Russia, Kyrgyzstan sign military agreement -agency.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Kyrgyzstan sign military agreement -agency.

text.p: Kyrgyzstan on Tuesday agreed to the continued stationing of Russian troops on its territory, fearing continued instability on the nearby Tajik-Afghan border, Russia's Interfax news agency said.

The director of Russia's Federal Border Service, Andrei Nikolayev, and Kyrgyz Defence Minister Myrzakan Subanov signed an accord extending the presence of Russian border guards along the former Soviet republic's frontier with Tajikistan.
Under the accord, Russia will also be able to use Kyrgyz military airfields "free of charge", the agency reported.

Nikolayev, cited by Interfax, warned that despite a peace accord to try to end a four-year civil war between the Tajik government and Islamic opposition guerrillas, Islamist fighters could "use the unstable situation in Tajikistan to increase their actions."
However, Nikolayev, on a tour of the former Soviet republics of Central Asia, said there were as yet no plans to strengthen the border with war-ravaged Afghanistan.
The Central Asian states voiced fears last month of an advance northwards towards their own borders by Afghanistan's purist Islamic Taleban militia.

Kyrgyz President Askar Akayev last week told visiting NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana that the republic shared Moscow's concerns over the western alliance's plans to expand eastwards and called Russia "our strategic partner".
